extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors querying literary agents / writers preparing query letters
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative expectations for writers preparing and submitting query letters to a literary agent, with emphasis on revision, following directions, and genre fit (crime fiction and narrative non-fiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Prepared! (aka Follow the Damn Directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be Prepared! (aka Follow the Damn Directions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit admonition to follow submission directions exactly — a concrete procedural expectation for writers querying an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Reachable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied expectation that the writer provides accurate contact information and is available for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Visible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests value in having a public presence or being discoverable (marketing/author platform implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre fit — agent specializations
rubrics_metrics.description: I specialize in crime fiction and narrative non-fiction (history and biography). I'll be glad to receive a query letter from you; guidelines to help you decide if I'm looking for what you write are below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent preference / filter: queries should match the agent's stated genres (crime fiction, narrative non-fiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to revise & resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for the many writers who embraced public critiques and sent revisions: "more of the 143 people who have embraced the public critiques of their work: more still of the 100+ who have sent revisions; more still of the 50+ who've sent second revisions; and I'm frankly awed by the one has sent five revisions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision is presented as a major positive quality — send revisions, iterate multiple times; revision is how writers learn and improve. The post frames revision as courageous and highly respected by the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in public critique (leave queries up)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author expresses greater respect for the 143 people who have embraced public critiques of their work and notes that some elected to have their queries taken down after critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving a queried submission publicly available for critique is valued as a learning resource for the community; taking queries down after critique is an option but is framed less favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common query mistakes ('query pitfalls' and 'annoy me')
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several posts labelled 'query pitfalls' and 'annoy me' that may help you avoid some common mistakes when querying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out and heed specific 'query pitfalls' and 'annoy me' guidance on the blog to avoid behaviors and errors that annoy agents or sink queries.
